title: Grateful Dead Live at Cleveland Public Hall on 1972-10-28

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1972 show famed for a smoking Dark Star and solid Attics of My Life, captured on a soundboard with generally good but occasionally uneven mix.
ai_review.review: The performance is celebrated for its powerful Dark Star (complete with the famous Phil‑O jam), tight drumming from Bill Kreutzmann, and standout moments like Attics of My Life and Greatest Story Ever Told.  The SBD source delivers a clear drum mix and good overall balance, though several listeners note muffled guitar and occasional mix glitches that make parts of the tape sound thin.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.1; most comments praise the show’s energy and Dark Star while noting some mix problems, yielding a solid 4‑star overall assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Drum mix is praised as front‑and‑center; Keith’s piano is clear.  Some reviewers report muffled Jerry guitar, uneven balance on certain tracks (Promised Land, Box of Rain) and occasional drop‑outs due to the cassette source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A classic late‑'72 setlist that moves from upbeat rockers to deep jams, with the second set anchored by a monster Dark Star and strong finishes.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Tight, after‑it guitar work on Dark Star praised; one reviewer complains his guitar is muffled in parts of the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass highlighted for a powerful ‘Philo Stomp’ during Dark Star; generally lauded as superb throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano described as wonderfully subdued and supportive, adding depth to the vocal harmonies.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drum mix is called fantastic—like he’s in the listener’s living room—and his jazz‑flavored playing on Dark Star receives high praise.
